column1: The library is words — trillions of pieces of text, like the ones you type.
The reading room is chips, thousands of them, running day and night for months.
And the teachers?
They're engineers.
India has the teachers.
You know this already.
Indian engineers write software for companies all over the world.
So your missing pieces are the library and the reading room.
Let's start with the library.
Almost nobody tells you about this part.
A lot of A.I. learns from the internet.
One of the biggest free copies of the web is called Common Crawl.
Many A.I. models learned from it, including an early model from the makers of the Chat G.P.T. you use.
So we took its latest copy, from October twenty twenty-six — more than two billion web pages — and checked its own count of languages.
English?
Forty-two out of every hundred pages.
Now, can you guess Hindi?
For every one page in Hindi... there are about two hundred pages in English.
And Hindi is the mother tongue of more than fifty crore people.
Marathi?
About fifteen hundred.
Telugu?
About two thousand three hundred.
And each of those is the mother tongue of around eight crore people, maybe yours.
All of India's languages together make up less than one page in every hundred.
Think about it.
More than one in every six people on Earth lives in your country.
But in the library these machines read, your language is almost invisible.
